text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has told visiting World Bank vice-president Jean-Michel Severino that Hanoi wants closer cooperation with the organisation.

-- Communist Party chief, Do Muoi, says that millions of Vietnamese, especially youths, will be mobilized through a compulsory labour scheme to reforest empty land and bare hills and develop the country.
-- An International trade fair, Vietnam EXPO'97, opened in Hanoi on Thursday with the participation of 150 foreign enterprises from 17 countries and 200 domestic enterprises.
-- Vietnam's State Bank Governor Cao Si Kiem has signed a $195.6 million credit agreement with the World Bank for the upgrading of a section of the main national north-south highway.
-- Vietnam has agreed to a meeting of experts in Beijing next week to discuss China's positioning of an oil rig in Vietnamese territorial waters.
-- Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko will visit Vietnam in late April to discuss measures aimed at strengthening economic, trade, science and technology cooperation.
